item.title: FSD false advertising case: Tesla must stop lying or it can’t sell cars, judge rules
item.description: A California judge ruled late Tuesday afternoon that Tesla engaged in “deceptive marketing” in reference to its Full Self-Driving system, and that Tesla’s license to sell and produce cars in the state should be revoked for 30 days. However, the California DMV has said it will give Tesla 60 days to comply and fix its marketing before going through with the suspension. more…

item.title: Jaguar believes it can sell $300,000 luxury EVs
item.description: Jaguar is betting on expensive luxury EVs, like the controversial Type 00, as part of its comeback plans. The struggling British automaker sees an opportunity in the 140,000 euro ($160,000) to 300,000 euro ($350,000) price range. more…

item.title: Tesla throws ‘cringe’ anti-union concert for Giga Berlin employees ahead of vote
item.description: Tesla has reportedly thrown a “Giga-Event” for its employees at Gigafactory Berlin, featuring German rapper Kool Savas. The goal? To rally the troops ahead of a critical union vote. The result? A “cringe” performance involving a Cybertruck, failed “Elon” chants, and some anti-union propaganda. more…

item.title: LAZ Parking plans EV chargers in 50,000 everyday parking spots
item.description: LAZ Parking, the largest privately owned parking operator in the US, is going all in on EV charging. It’s made a strategic investment in Silicon Valley–based Epic Charging, with a plan to roll out up to 50,000 Level 2 EV chargers across LAZ’s parking portfolio in the US and Canada. more…

item.title: 25% of new cars sold globally in 2025 were EVs – here’s who bought them
item.description: More than 25% of new cars sold globally in 2025 are now electric, according to new analysis from energy think tank Ember. This growth is increasingly driven by emerging markets that, only a few years ago, had minimal adoption of EVs. more…
